\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اعتصاب} (e'tesâb)}{اعتصاب (e'tesâb)}]{\fa{اعتصاب} (e'tesâb) — a strike}

\label{lesson:FA-C384-etesab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rival, then the Persian for advertising.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اعتصاب}}
\textbf{\fa{اعتصاب}} (\emph{e'tesâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}a strike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارگرها} \fa{برای} \fa{حقوق} \fa{بیشتر} \fa{اعتصاب} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kârgarhâ barâye hoquq-e bishtar e'tesâb kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers went on strike for higher pay.
\end{quote}

\emph{E'tesâb kardan} — to go on strike. Plural \emph{e'tesâbât}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اعتصاب}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{i'tiṣāb} (EtymDB), a verbal noun usually explained as banding together; in modern Persian it is a strike.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{e'tesâb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{e'tesâb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a rival, then the Persian for advertising, then say \emph{e'tesâb} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتحادیه} (ettehâdiye)}{اتحادیه (ettehâdiye)}]{\fa{اتحادیه} (ettehâdiye) — a union, an association}

\label{lesson:FA-C384-ettehadiye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for advertising, then the Persian for a strike.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتحادیه}}
\textbf{\fa{اتحادیه}} (\emph{ettehâdiye}) — \textquotedblleft{}a union, an association\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتحادیه} \fa{کارگران} \fa{با} \fa{مدیرها} \fa{مذاکره} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ettehâdiye-ye kârgarân bâ modirhâ mozâkere kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers' union negotiated with the managers.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ettehâd} \textquotedblleft{}unity\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-iye}. \emph{Ettehâdiye-ye kârgari} — a trade union.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اتحادیه}} is built on \emph{ettehâd} \textquotedblleft{}unity\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{ittiḥād} \textquotedblleft{}becoming one\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-iye}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ettehâdiye}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ettehâdiye}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for advertising, then the Persian for a strike, then say \emph{ettehâdiye} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زحمت} \fa{کشیدن} (zahmat keshidan)}{زحمت کشیدن (zahmat keshidan)}]{\fa{زحمت} \fa{کشیدن} (zahmat keshidan) — to work hard, to take pains}

\label{lesson:FA-C384-zahmat-keshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a strike, then the Persian for a union.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زحمت} \fa{کشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{زحمت} \fa{کشیدن}} (\emph{zahmat keshidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to work hard, to take pains\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{برای} \fa{ما} \fa{خیلی} \fa{زحمت} \fa{کشید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram barâye mâ kheyli zahmat keshid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother worked very hard for us.
\end{quote}

\emph{Zahmat} \textquotedblleft{}trouble, effort\textquotedblright{} + \emph{keshidan} \textquotedblleft{}to pull\textquotedblright{} (stem \emph{kesh-}). A polite thanks: \emph{zahmat keshidid}, you went to a lot of trouble.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{زحمت}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{zaḥma} \textquotedblleft{}pressing, thronging\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); with the inherited Persian verb \emph{keshidan} \textquotedblleft{}to pull, to bear\textquotedblright{}, it means to bear the trouble.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zahmat keshidan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zahmat keshidan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{zahmat keshidan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a strike, then the Persian for a union, then say \emph{zahmat keshidan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{زحمت} \fa{کشیدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To work hard, to take pains\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{موفق} \fa{شدن} (movaffaq shodan)}{موفق شدن (movaffaq shodan)}]{\fa{موفق} \fa{شدن} (movaffaq shodan) — to succeed}

\label{lesson:FA-C384-movaffaq-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a union, then the Persian for to work hard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{موفق} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{موفق} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{movaffaq shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to succeed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بالاخره} \fa{در} \fa{امتحان} \fa{موفق} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâlâkhare dar emtehân movaffaq shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end she passed the exam.
\end{quote}

\emph{Movaffaq} \textquotedblleft{}successful\textquotedblright{} + \emph{shodan}. \emph{Dar chizi movaffaq shodan} — to succeed in something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{موفق} \fa{شدن}} joins \emph{movaffaq} \textquotedblleft{}successful\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{muwaffaq} \textquotedblleft{}granted success\textquotedblright{}, to the inherited Persian verb \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{movaffaq shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{movaffaq shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a union, then the Persian for to work hard, then say \emph{movaffaq shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شکست} \fa{خوردن} (shekast khordan)}{شکست خوردن (shekast khordan)}]{\fa{شکست} \fa{خوردن} (shekast khordan) — to be defeated, to lose}

\label{lesson:FA-C384-shekast-khordan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to work hard, then the Persian for to succeed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شکست} \fa{خوردن}}
\textbf{\fa{شکست} \fa{خوردن}} (\emph{shekast khordan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be defeated, to lose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تیم} \fa{ما} \fa{در} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{شکست} \fa{خورد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tim-e mâ dar mosâbeqe shekast khord.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our team was defeated in the match.
\end{quote}

\emph{Shekast} \textquotedblleft{}defeat\textquotedblright{} + \emph{khordan} \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{} (stem \emph{khor-}): literally to eat a defeat.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{شکست} \fa{خوردن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{shekast}, the past stem of \emph{shekastan} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian \emph{škastan} and PIE \emph{skeyd-}, and \emph{khordan} \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{}, inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
